title: Patient Rail
user: Roguelike players who enjoy browser accessibility but want a thoughtful, turn-based 20-minute daily run instead of reflex-heavy 'ASCII plus deaths' play.

evidence.quote_or_summary: A player argues that roguelikes need more than ASCII graphics and frequent death, and says the real-time, constantly messaging experience felt Flappy-Bird-like rather than contemplative.
The fetched itch.io page is the live Risk of Train browser-roguelike page attached to the HN discussion.

recurrence: The feedback is a precise genre critique from an active player: browser roguelike availability is not enough if it loses deliberation and readable decision space.
current_workaround: Play a desktop traditional roguelike, tolerate real-time browser action, or use a generic daily puzzle instead of a tactical run.
incumbents_and_gap: Brogue and desktop roguelikes preserve thought but are less link-friendly; action browser roguelikes prioritize immediacy. A daily, turn-based micro-roguelike can serve the gap without attempting a full content universe.
smallest_useful_product: A 20-minute daily train-defense run on a 7x7 grid: one action per turn, one visible enemy intent each turn, and three route stops. The daily seed changes car layouts, enemy families, and a final weather rule. Non-goals: real-time combat, procedural lore generation, account progression, or multiplayer.
success_measure: Median time spent on a decision is above three seconds without a fall in completion rate below 35%, and 20% of players return for three daily seeds.
monetization: one-time — a finite tactical game should ship complete; a free daily seed can lead to a paid offline/archive edition.
constraints: All seeds must be solvable/finishable under defined rules; keyboard-first and screen-reader action labels; no copyrighted train/game-world assets.
why_distinct: It treats contemplation, intent visibility, and a daily bounded run as the core experience rather than using roguelike aesthetics for an action game.
